post.caption: Vulcanite is rubber hardened into jewelry. Heating rubber with sulfur is called vulcanizing, after the god Vulcan. Charles Goodyear discovered the process in 1839. The popular story says a rubber mix touched a hot stove. Far more sulfur and longer heating turns rubber hard and dense. That hard black form is called ebonite, after ebony wood. By the 1850s it was a popular, cheaper substitute for jet. It was molded into brooches and bracelets, so identical pieces turn up. Light slowly fades the black toward brown. Rub it or warm it and it gives off a sulfur smell.
